# `@sandbox-kit/blaxel`

Blaxel provider for [`@sandbox-kit/sandbox`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sandbox-kit/sandbox).
Pass `blaxel()` into `new Client({ provider, ... })`.

## Install

```sh
npm install @sandbox-kit/sandbox @sandbox-kit/blaxel
```

Requires Node.js 20, 22, or 24.15+, a Blaxel API key, and a workspace name.

## Quick start

```ts
import { blaxel } from "@sandbox-kit/blaxel";
import { Client } from "@sandbox-kit/sandbox";

const workspace = process.env.BL_WORKSPACE?.trim();

await using client = new Client({
  provider: blaxel(),
  auth: { apiKey: { key: process.env.BL_API_KEY! } },
  ...(workspace ? { scope: { workspace } } : {}),
  region: process.env.BL_REGION ?? "us-pdx-1",
  timeout: 120_000,
});

const sandbox = await client.create({
  name: "kit-example",
  source: { image: { reference: "blaxel/base-image:latest" } },
  resources: { memoryMib: 4096n },
  lifetime: { maximumLifetime: 24 * 60 * 60_000 },
});
console.log(sandbox.id); // same as create name; use with get / BL_SANDBOX_NAME
```

Closing the client releases local resources only. Reclaim sandboxes with TTL /
idle policies or `delete`.

## Configuration

| Setting        | Notes                                                   |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| API key        | `auth: { apiKey: { key } }`                             |
| Omitted `auth` | Uses `BL_API_KEY` / `BL_WORKSPACE` from the environment |
| Workspace      | `scope.workspace` — or `BL_WORKSPACE` when omitted      |
| Region         | `region` — required for create                          |
| Endpoint       | Not supported                                           |

Token-pair, bearer, and OAuth are rejected. Only `scope.workspace` is accepted
on scope.

Use one Blaxel configuration per process. A second client with different
credentials or workspace is rejected.

## What you can do

### Create

Required: a valid `name`, an image, and `region`.

- Name: blank or whitespace-only is rejected; lowercase alphanumeric with
  single hyphens; max 49 characters.
- Optional: `memoryMib`, labels, environment, ports, outbound domains,
  max-age TTL (≥5 minutes), idle-delete (≥1 minute).
- Not supported: idle disable, runtime, isolation, volumes, CPU/disk
  overrides (Blaxel derives CPU from memory).

Pass memory in MiB, or omit it for Blaxel’s default. Labels on `info()` appear
only when Blaxel reports them.

Set client or create `timeout` for how long create may wait. With a 1–50s
timeout, a timed-out create frees the name. Ready, Started, and Submitted wait
are not supported. Ports 80, 443, and 8080 are reserved. Default port
transport is HTTP; plain is TCP; TLS is TLS; HTTP/2 over TLS is not supported.

If Blaxel’s edge returns HTTP 504 during create, the client may keep waiting
until the sandbox is ready or your create timeout ends. A timeout does not
always mean the sandbox was never created — call `get` by name before
recreating.

If the name already exists, you get `AlreadyExists`.

### Lifecycle

Available: `get` / `refresh` (by name), `delete`, and `close`. `close` does
not delete the sandbox. Start, stop, pause, archive, terminate, and attach are
not available.

After a successful `delete`, `state` is `deleted` and `terminal` is true.
Omit `wait` to return as soon as Blaxel accepts the delete — recreating the
same name too soon may return `Conflict`. Pass `wait: true` to wait until
removal finishes.

### Filesystem

Methods: `readFile`, `writeFile`, `copyFromLocal`, `copyToLocal`,
`makeDirectory`, `listDirectory`, `stat`, and `remove`. Paths must be absolute.
`parents` defaults to true; `parents: false` is not supported.

`stat` returns `type` (file or directory), `size`, and usually `permissions`,
`owner`, `group`, and `modifiedAt`. `name` and `path` are whatever Blaxel
reports. Missing local files for `copyFromLocal`, and local write failures from
`copyToLocal`, use field `local_path`.

### Process

`sandbox.process.run` waits until the command finishes. Set exactly one of
`argv` or `shell`. A non-zero exit code is not an error — check `exitCode`.
You get both stdout and stderr.

Omit or zero `timeout` to wait without a Blaxel process time limit (your
signal can still abort). A positive timeout must be whole seconds (`2000` is
two seconds; `1500` is rejected) and caps how long the command may run.
Aborting the signal stops waiting; the remote command may keep running. If the
wait times out, you get a timeout error.

### Errors you will see

| Situation                                  | Kind              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| Create when the name already exists        | `AlreadyExists`   |
| Conflict while a delete is still finishing | `Conflict`        |
| Lifetime below floor or not whole seconds  | `InvalidArgument` |
| Unsupported create field (runtime, …)      | `Unsupported`     |

Blaxel control-plane codes appear on `providerCode` when present.

## Examples

| Example       | Project                                                                                                                              |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Creation      | [create-blaxel-sandbox](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/blaxel/configuration/create-blaxel-sandbox) |
| Run a command | [run-blaxel-command](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/blaxel/process/run-blaxel-command)             |
| Process       | [process examples](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/blaxel/process)                                  |
| Read a file   | [read-blaxel-file](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/blaxel/filesystem/read-blaxel-file)              |
| Filesystem    | [filesystem examples](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/blaxel/filesystem)                            |
| Retrieval     | [get-blaxel-sandbox](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/blaxel/lifecycle/get-blaxel-sandbox)           |
| Delete        | [delete-blaxel-sandbox](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript/blaxel/lifecycle/delete-blaxel-sandbox)     |
| Full index    | [TypeScript examples](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/typescript)                                              |

# Blaxel

Create and manage Blaxel sandboxes with the shared sandbox client.

Requires Go 1.26.0 or later and a Blaxel API key. Set `Auth` to an API key and
`Scope.Workspace` to the workspace name. If either is omitted, the client uses
`BL_API_KEY` and `BL_WORKSPACE` from the environment when present.
`Config.Region` is required for create.

## Install

```sh
go get github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox@latest
go get github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/providers/blaxel@latest
```

## Create a sandbox

```go
config := &sandbox.Config{
	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.APIKey{
		ApiKey: &sandbox.APIKeyCredentials{Key: os.Getenv("BL_API_KEY")},
	}},
	Region:  sandbox.Value("us-pdx-1"),
	Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Minute),
}
if workspace := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("BL_WORKSPACE")); workspace != "" {
	config.Scope = &sandbox.Scope{Workspace: sandbox.Value(workspace)}
}
client, err := sandbox.NewClient(blaxel.New(), config)
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
defer client.Close(context.Background())

instance, err := client.Create(context.Background(), &sandbox.CreateOptions{
	Name: sandbox.Value("my-sandbox"),
	Source: &sandbox.SandboxSource{Kind: &sandbox.Image{
		Image: &sandbox.ImageSource{Reference: "blaxel/base-image:latest"},
	}},
})
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(instance.ID())
```

Create requires a name and an image. `ID()` is that name — use it with `Get`
and example env `BL_SANDBOX_NAME`. Closing the client does not delete the
sandbox. Call `Delete`, or set a lifetime policy.

## Settings

| Setting   | How to set it                         |
| --------- | ------------------------------------- |
| API key   | `Auth` with `APIKey`                  |
| Workspace | `Scope.Workspace` (or `BL_WORKSPACE`) |
| Region    | `Config.Region` (required for create) |
| Timeout   | `Config.Timeout` (create/op deadline) |

`Config.Endpoint` is not supported. Token pair, OAuth, and bearer auth are
rejected. `Scope` fields other than `Workspace` are rejected.

## What you can do

### Create

Required: a name and an image. Name is required (blank or whitespace-only is
rejected). Names are lowercase alphanumeric with single hyphens (max 49
characters).

Optional: labels, environment, memory, ports, outbound domains, maximum
lifetime (≥5 minutes), and idle terminate (≥1 minute).

Not supported: idle disable, runtime, isolation, volumes, CPU/disk overrides
(Blaxel derives CPU from memory). Ports 80, 443, and 8080 are reserved.
Default port transport is HTTP; plain is TCP; TLS is TLS; HTTP/2 over TLS is
not supported.

Pass memory with `Resources.MemoryMib`, or omit it for Blaxel’s default.
`Info().Labels` appears only when Blaxel reports labels.

Set client or create timeout for how long create may wait. With a 1–50s
timeout, a timed-out create frees the name. Ready, Started, and Submitted wait
and readiness probes are not supported.

If Blaxel’s edge returns HTTP 504 during create, the call returns a timeout as
soon as that response arrives. A timeout does not always mean the sandbox was
never created — call `Get` by name before recreating.

If the name already exists, you get `AlreadyExists`.

### Lifecycle

Available: `Get`, `Refresh`, `Delete`, and `Close`. Lookup is by name
(`ID()` equals the create name). Attach, start, stop, pause, archive, and
terminate are not available. `Close` only drops the local handle.

After a successful `Delete`, `Info().State` is `Deleted` and `Terminal` is
true. Omit `Wait` to return as soon as Blaxel accepts the delete — recreating
the same name too soon may return `Conflict`. Pass `Wait: true` to wait until
removal finishes.

### Filesystem

Methods: read, write, copy in/out, mkdir, list, stat, and remove. Paths must
be absolute. `Parents` defaults to true; `Parents: false` is not supported.

`Stat` returns `Type` (file or directory), `Size`, and usually `Permissions`,
`Owner`, `Group`, and `ModifiedAt`. `Name` and `Path` are whatever Blaxel
reports. Missing local files for `CopyFromLocal`, and local write failures from
`CopyToLocal`, use field `local_path`.

### Process

`Process().Run` runs one command and waits for it to finish. Set exactly one of
`Argv` or `Shell`. A non-zero exit code is not an error — read `GetExitCode`.
You get both stdout and stderr.

Omit or zero `Timeout` to wait without a Blaxel process time limit (your
context can still cancel). A positive timeout must be whole seconds and caps
how long the command may run. Canceling the context stops waiting; the remote
command may keep running. If the wait times out, you get a timeout error.

### Errors you will see

| Situation                                  | Kind              |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| Create when the name already exists        | `AlreadyExists`   |
| Conflict while a delete is still finishing | `Conflict`        |
| Lifetime below floor or not whole seconds  | `InvalidArgument` |
| Unsupported create field (runtime, …)      | `Unsupported`     |

Blaxel control-plane codes appear on `ProviderCode` when present.

## Examples

| Operation                | Program                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Create                   | [create-blaxel-sandbox](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/blaxel/configuration/create-blaxel-sandbox) |
| Run a command            | [run-blaxel-command](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/blaxel/process/run-blaxel-command)             |
| Shell / cwd / env / exit | [process examples](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/blaxel/process)                                  |
| Read a file              | [read-blaxel-file](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/blaxel/filesystem/read-blaxel-file)              |
| Filesystem               | [filesystem examples](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/blaxel/filesystem)                            |
| Look up                  | [get-blaxel-sandbox](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/blaxel/lifecycle/get-blaxel-sandbox)           |
| Delete                   | [delete-blaxel-sandbox](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go/blaxel/lifecycle/delete-blaxel-sandbox)     |
| All                      | [Go examples](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/tree/main/examples/go)                                                      |

# Providers

Install the core package and the provider you use.

|            | Daytona                                                                  | Modal                                                                  | Blaxel                                                                  |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| TypeScript | `@sandbox-kit/sandbox` and `@sandbox-kit/daytona`                        | `@sandbox-kit/sandbox` and `@sandbox-kit/modal`                        | `@sandbox-kit/sandbox` and `@sandbox-kit/blaxel`                        |
| Go         | `github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox` and `.../providers/daytona` | `github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox` and `.../providers/modal` | `github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/sdks/go/sandbox` and `.../providers/blaxel` |

## TypeScript

```ts
await using client = new Client({
  provider: modal(),
  auth: { tokenPair: { id: tokenId, secret: tokenSecret } },
  scope: { appName: "existing-app" },
});
```

```ts
await using client = new Client({
  provider: blaxel(),
  auth: { apiKey: { key: apiKey } },
  scope: { workspace: "my-workspace" },
  region: "us-pdx-1",
});
```

Use one Blaxel configuration per process. A client with different credentials
or workspace is rejected.

## Go

```go
client, err := sandbox.NewClient(modal.New(), &sandbox.Config{
	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{
		Credentials: &sandbox.TokenPair{
			TokenPair: &sandbox.TokenPairCredentials{Id: tokenID, Secret: tokenSecret},
		},
	},
	Scope: &sandbox.Scope{AppName: sandbox.Value("existing-app")},
})
```

```go
client, err := sandbox.NewClient(blaxel.New(), &sandbox.Config{
	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{
		Credentials: &sandbox.APIKey{
			ApiKey: &sandbox.APIKeyCredentials{Key: apiKey},
		},
	},
	Scope:  &sandbox.Scope{Workspace: sandbox.Value("my-workspace")},
	Region: sandbox.Value("us-pdx-1"),
})
```

## What each provider can do

| Operation                   | Modal                              | Daytona                                    | Blaxel                                 |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------- |
| Create                      | Registry image and an existing app | Default snapshot, named snapshot, or image | Named image create (Blaxel name rules) |
| Open an existing sandbox    | `attach` (ID only)                 | `get` (provider lookup)                    | `get` / `refresh` by name              |
| Start, stop, pause, archive | Unsupported                        | Supported                                  | Unsupported                            |
| Delete                      | Unsupported                        | Supported                                  | Supported                              |
| Terminate                   | Supported                          | Unsupported                                | Unsupported                            |
| Filesystem                  | Same eight shared methods          | Same eight shared methods                  | Same eight shared methods              |
| Process                     | Same blocking `Run`                | Same blocking `Run`                        | Same blocking `Run`                    |

`supports` / `Supports` reports whether the provider implements that operation.
A missing operation fails before the provider call. Daytona may still reject a
supported call for a particular sandbox.

### Placement

- **Daytona** — set the target with `region` on the client. Placement on the
  create request is rejected.
- **Modal** — set cloud and region on the create request. A placement target
  on the client is rejected.
- **Blaxel** — `region` on the client is required for create. Per-request
  placement is rejected.

Closing the client closes your connection to the provider. The sandboxes keep
running. Closing a handle leaves the sandbox as it is.

GPU requests, resizing, storage volumes, browsers, streaming process handles,
sessions, PTY, and macOS or Windows creation are outside this API.

See [configuration](configuration.md), [creation](sandbox-creation.md),
[lifecycle](sandbox-lifecycle.md), [filesystem](filesystem.md), and
[process](process.md).

# Client configuration

Pass a provider and shared settings to the client.

## TypeScript

Invalid settings throw at construction. Timeouts are milliseconds.

```ts
await using client = new Client({
  provider: daytona(),
  auth: { apiKey: { key: process.env.DAYTONA_API_KEY! } },
  timeout: 120_000,
});
```

Call `await client.close()`, or prefer `await using`. That closes your
connection to the provider. Sandboxes keep running. Closing one handle does
not close the client.

Auth is one nested shape: `auth: { apiKey: { key } }`, `tokenPair`,
`bearerToken`, or `oauthRefresh`.

Use one Blaxel configuration per process. A client with different credentials
or workspace is rejected.

A TypeScript config is a plain object, so `JSON.stringify` includes credential
fields — keep it out of logs.

## Go

`NewClient` returns `(*Client, error)`.

```go
client, err := sandbox.NewClient(daytona.New(), &sandbox.Config{
	Auth: &sandbox.AuthConfig{Credentials: &sandbox.APIKey{
		ApiKey: &sandbox.APIKeyCredentials{Key: os.Getenv("DAYTONA_API_KEY")},
	}},
	Timeout: sandbox.Duration(2 * time.Minute),
})
```

Call `client.Close(ctx)`. That closes your connection to the provider.
Sandboxes keep running. Closing one handle does not close the client.

## Configuration fields

| Setting    | Purpose                                               |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Provider   | Daytona, Modal, or Blaxel constructor                 |
| Auth       | One credential shape. Omit to use provider env creds  |
| Scope      | App, environment, organization, project, or workspace |
| Endpoint   | Provider API URL, where supported                     |
| Region     | Provider target or default placement                  |
| Timeout    | Default deadline for calls that omit their own        |

Changing the config object after you create the client does not change the
client.

## Provider support

| Setting          | Modal                                                      | Daytona                           | Blaxel                         |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| API key          | Unsupported                                                | Supported                         | Supported                      |
| Token pair       | Supported                                                  | Unsupported                       | Unsupported                    |
| Bearer/JWT token | Unsupported                                                | Supported; organization required  | Unsupported                    |
| OAuth refresh    | Refresh token, client ID, and one client secret or JWT key | Unsupported                       | Unsupported                    |
| Endpoint         | Unsupported                                                | API URL                           | Unsupported                    |
| Region           | Default sandbox region preference                          | Target                            | Required for create            |
| App name         | Required for app lookup                                    | Unsupported                       | Unsupported                    |
| Environment      | Client, app, and secret lookup environment                 | Unsupported                       | Unsupported                    |
| Organization ID  | Unsupported                                                | Organization                      | Unsupported                    |
| Project ID       | Unsupported                                                | Unsupported                       | Unsupported                    |
| Workspace        | Unsupported                                                | Unsupported                       | Blaxel workspace (`BL_WORKSPACE` when omitted) |

A setting the provider does not support fails before the provider client is
created. Omit auth when the provider should use credentials from the
environment.

### Daytona endpoints

A remote endpoint uses HTTPS. HTTP is accepted for `localhost` or a loopback
address. A URL with a username, password, or fragment is rejected. Daytona
uses `endpoint` when you set it, otherwise `https://app.daytona.io/api`. Kit
does not read a Daytona endpoint from the environment.

Construction does not check that credentials work. The provider checks on the
first create or open.

## Deadlines

The client timeout is the default deadline. Create and lifecycle calls can
override it. Explicit zero means no deadline from the client. A context
deadline or abort signal that fires earlier still wins.

### Daytona

Create keeps its 60-second default when the timeout is omitted or zero.
Start, stop, pause, and delete use that 60-second default when omitted, and
treat explicit zero as no operation timeout.

### Blaxel

Set a client or create timeout for how long create may wait.

**TypeScript.** If Blaxel’s edge returns HTTP 504 during create, the client
may keep waiting until the sandbox is ready or that timeout ends. A timeout
does not always mean the sandbox was never created — call `get` by name
before recreating.

**Go.** If Blaxel’s edge returns HTTP 504 during create, the call returns a
timeout as soon as that response arrives. Call `Get` by name before
recreating.

## Credentials

Keep configuration out of logs and stored files. Construction, operation, and
cleanup failures use the same error details. See
[responses and errors](responses-and-errors.md).

See [Go examples](../examples/go/README.md) and
[TypeScript examples](../examples/typescript/README.md).

# Sandbox creation

Create returns a sandbox handle. Creation settings are separate from lifecycle
calls on an existing sandbox.

## TypeScript

```ts
const sandbox = await client.create(options, { timeout: 60_000 });
```

Create options use nested exclusive fields (`source: { image: … }`,
`readiness: { tcpPort }` or `{ command }`), plain `environment` / `labels`
maps, and millisecond durations. A missing property means the field was
omitted.

## Go

```go
instance, err := client.Create(ctx, options)
```

Use `sandbox.Value(v)` for optional scalars (including zero or false) and
`sandbox.Duration(d)` for timeouts.

## Supported creation settings

| Setting                | Modal                                                                                  | Daytona                                                      | Blaxel                                                                          |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Source                 | Explicit registry image and an existing app                                            | Default/specified snapshot or registry image                 | Named create (Blaxel name rules); registry image required                       |
| Runtime                | Entrypoint, absolute working directory, PTY                                            | Toolbox language and user                                    | Unsupported                                                                     |
| Isolation              | Default, gVisor container, Linux VM                                                    | Nested KVM flag; class inherited from source                 | Unsupported                                                                     |
| Resources              | Fractional CPU, CPU limit, memory request/limit                                        | Whole CPU and GiB memory/disk; image required for overrides  | Memory in MiB; CPU/disk overrides not supported                                 |
| Placement              | Cloud and region preferences                                                           | Client target; request placement unsupported                 | Client `region` required; request placement unsupported                         |
| Environment and labels | Environment map and tags                                                               | Environment map and labels                                   | Environment map and labels                                                      |
| Security               | Named secrets and workload identity                                                    | Egress-placeholder secrets and public access                 | Unsupported                                                                     |
| Network                | Egress allowlists, inbound CIDRs, private network, managed proxy, ports, custom domain | Egress allowlists, outbound proxy, linked sandbox            | Ports (not 80/443/8080; default → HTTP); outbound domains                       |
| Lifetime               | Maximum lifetime and idle termination                                                  | TTL, ephemeral, stop/pause/archive/delete policies           | Maximum lifetime (≥5m) and idle terminate (≥1m); idle disable not supported     |
| Observability          | Verbose output                                                                         | Telemetry endpoint                                           | Unsupported                                                                     |

Volumes are not available on create for any provider.

Unsupported fields fail before the provider call. The error names the field
(for example `resources.disk_mib`).

### Wait behavior

**Modal.** Default or scheduled wait. Ready wait needs a probe and a positive
create timeout.

**Daytona (TypeScript).** Default or started wait. Submitted wait is not
supported — create returns after startup.

**Daytona (Go).** Default, submitted, or started wait.

**Blaxel.** Ready, Started, and Submitted wait are not supported. Set a create
timeout; with 1–50 seconds, a timed-out create frees the name.

**Blaxel TypeScript.** If the edge returns HTTP 504 during create, the client
may keep waiting until the sandbox is ready or the create timeout ends. Call
`get` by name before recreating.

**Blaxel Go.** If the edge returns HTTP 504 during create, the call returns a
timeout as soon as that response arrives. Call `Get` by name before recreating.

## Units and limits

Omitted fields keep the provider default. Invalid combinations fail in the
client before the provider call.

| Resource         | Modal                                           | Daytona                                      | Blaxel                                      |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| CPU              | Physical cores; minimum 0.125, precision 0.001  | Whole CPU cores                              | Derived by Blaxel from memory; overrides rejected |
| Memory           | MiB; minimum request 128                        | Whole GiB expressed as MiB                   | Pass memory in MiB; omit for Blaxel default |
| Disk             | Creation override unsupported                   | Whole GiB expressed as MiB                   | Creation override unsupported               |
| Maximum lifetime | Positive whole seconds, up to 24 hours (TS: ms) | Whole-minute TTL (TS: ms); zero disables TTL | At least 5 minutes when set                 |

Account quotas, image existence, regions, and capacity remain
provider-enforced. Resources and labels on the handle are what the provider
reported.

## Policy semantics

| Mode     | Meaning                                      |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| Default  | Defer to the provider                        |
| Disabled | Explicitly disable that policy               |
| After    | Apply after a delay (zero = immediate action)|

TypeScript delays are milliseconds.

### Daytona

| Action          | Disabled    | After zero  | Positive delay                 |
| --------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| Idle stop       | Native zero | Rejected    | Whole minutes                  |
| Idle pause      | Native zero | Rejected    | Whole minutes                  |
| Stopped archive | Rejected    | Rejected    | Whole minutes, at most 30 days |
| Stopped delete  | Rejected    | Native zero | Whole minutes                  |

Positive stop and pause delays are mutually exclusive. Ephemeral cannot combine
with positive pause, archive, or delayed-delete. Linked sandboxes must be
ephemeral.

### Modal

Idle termination supports disabled or positive whole-second delays. Maximum
lifetime and idle delay are separate settings.

### Blaxel

Idle terminate supports only After with a delay of at least 1m, or provider
default. Disabled idle terminate is rejected. Maximum lifetime, when set, must
be at least 5m. Ephemeral, idle stop/pause, stopped archive/delete, runtime,
and isolation are rejected.

## Networking

A present empty allowlist means deny-all. Empty inbound Modal allowlists and
empty Daytona allowlists are rejected. Secrets are references to
provider-managed secrets, not authentication credentials.

## Results and cleanup

`info()` / `Info()` returns a copy. Editing that copy leaves the handle
unchanged. Closing the client or handle does not delete the sandbox.

Lifecycle: [lifecycle guide](sandbox-lifecycle.md). Files:
[filesystem](filesystem.md). Commands: [process](process.md).

# Sandbox lifecycle

Lifecycle methods operate on a handle from `Create`, a provider-verified
`Get`, or Modal `Attach`. They do not reuse the creation request.

## TypeScript

```ts
await using client = new Client(config);
const sandbox = await client.create(request);
if (!sandbox.supports(LifecycleCapability.Stop)) {
  throw new Error(`sandbox ${sandbox.id} cannot be stopped`);
}
await sandbox.stop({ timeout: 60_000 });
```

Clients and handles implement `AsyncDisposable`. Prefer `await using` when the
lifetime matches the block. Timeouts are milliseconds.

Abort rejects the `await`. The handle stays busy until the provider call
settles, so the next call on the same handle does not overlap it.

## Go

```go
instance, err := client.Create(ctx, options)
if err != nil {
	return err
}
if !instance.Supports(sandbox.LifecycleCapabilityStop) {
	return fmt.Errorf("sandbox %s cannot be stopped", instance.ID())
}
return instance.Stop(ctx, &sandbox.StopOptions{Timeout: sandbox.Duration(time.Minute)})
```

Cancel or a deadline on the context ends the wait. The handle stays busy until
the provider call returns.

## Timeouts

An operation-specific timeout overrides the client default. Omitted timeout
inherits the client deadline. Explicit zero adds no client deadline.

**Daytona.** Start, stop, pause, and delete use a native 60-second default when
the timeout is omitted. Explicit zero means no operation timeout. Non-whole
seconds are rejected.

**Modal.** A terminate timeout is how long the SDK waits. With wait, Modal
polls until the sandbox exits or the deadline fires.

## Close

`client.close()` / `Client.Close` closes your connection to the provider. It
does not stop or delete the sandbox.

`sandbox.close()` / `Sandbox.Close` releases local handle resources only. You
can keep using the handle afterward for Daytona and Blaxel local close; Modal
close does not terminate the sandbox.

## Operation meanings

| Method    | Meaning                                                              |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Start     | Enter the running state from a retained state                        |
| Stop      | Request a stop (ephemeral policy may still destroy the sandbox)      |
| Pause     | Memory-preserving transition; inspect returned metadata for state    |
| Terminate | Permanently finish execution; does not promise record deletion       |
| Archive   | Move retained state to archive storage                               |
| Delete    | Irreversibly remove the provider sandbox                             |

Unsupported operations return `Unsupported` before a provider call.
`supports` / `Supports` checks whether the provider implements an operation.

Prefer portable `state` / `State` and `terminal` / `Terminal` on the handle.
A later lifecycle call still goes to the provider.

## Provider support

| Operation   | Modal                                  | Daytona     | Blaxel                             |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Attach      | Supported; ID only, no provider lookup | Unsupported | Unsupported                        |
| Refresh/Get | Unsupported                            | Supported   | Supported (lookup by sandbox name) |
| Start       | Unsupported                            | Supported   | Unsupported                        |
| Stop        | Unsupported                            | Supported   | Unsupported                        |
| Pause       | Unsupported                            | Supported   | Unsupported                        |
| Terminate   | Supported                              | Unsupported | Unsupported                        |
| Archive     | Unsupported                            | Supported   | Unsupported                        |
| Delete      | Unsupported                            | Supported   | Supported                          |

### Daytona

Whether a sandbox accepts pause, archive, or stop is Daytona’s decision.

### Modal

`Terminate` is not presented as stop or delete. `Attach` builds a handle from
an id with no remote lookup. `Get` and `Refresh` are not available.

### Blaxel

Lookup is by name for `Get` and `Refresh`. After a successful `Delete`,
`state` is deleted and `terminal` is true. Omit wait to return when Blaxel
accepts the delete; recreating the same name too soon may return `Conflict`.
Pass wait to wait until removal finishes. Attach, start, stop, pause, archive,
and terminate are not available.

File calls: [filesystem](filesystem.md).
